title: Musicians' brotherhood, baseball and softball
summary: He recalls Armstrong and Hines playing baseball in Washington Park and the DeLisa bands playing softball against Woody Herman's team after work.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Yeah, real brotherhood, right. And that's what I liked -- I told you about Kansas City. You played there, everybody loved you. And then, this town was the same way. The guys like Louis Armstrong, that was a great sight. Louis Armstrong and Earl Hines and all of these guys out in the Washington Park out there, playing baseball, with his big fat self. And it was real joy and they were getting real kicks out of it, a musicians' thing.
Maybe we need some more hard times or something.
Oh, yeah, right, because in later years, in the later years, we played softball, when I was at the Delisa and we would get off at 6:00 in the morning, and
then go change clothes and go out to the park and play softball. And we played teams like Woody Herman and they would get up in the morning and come on out and play.
Right, all of them had a softball team.
